Power-Aware Orchestration for Geo-Distributed LLM Inference via Quantum Optimization
results.abstract: For geo-distributed large-scale LLM inference, achieving lowlatency request execution requires jointly optimizing transmission delay, heterogeneous compute capacity, and spatialtemporal variability in power availability across datacenters. We formulate this orchestration problem as an integer linear program that minimizes end-to-end latency while explicitly capturing time-to-first-token, per-token generation latency, and wide-area network delay. However, the resulting problem is NP-hard and intractable for real-time decision-making at scale. To address this challenge, we develop a quantum-classical hybrid optimization framework based on the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA). We introduce a feasibility-guaranteed QAOA (FG-QAOA), which incorporates structured variable pruning to eliminate infeasible routing configurations while preserving the optimal solution space. This reduction yields a compact formulation that is then transformed into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization model with penalty-encoded constraints, enabling mapping to an Ising Hamiltonian for quantum optimization. Experimental results show that FG-QAOA achieves near-optimal performance, matching the exact solver on small-scale instances while keeping the optimality gap below 3.1% on larger instances, and exhibiting much slower runtime growth than the exact solver.
